data.title: Centered Column
data.tagline: Keep one narrow content column centered on the page
data.description: A centered column focuses attention on reading or one simple task such as signing in, composing a post, or changing settings. Set a comfortable maximum width and keep supporting actions nearby. It is not suitable for dense dashboards that need side-by-side comparison.

avoid: Place wide tables in a narrow column
Let the column grow too wide on large screens
Use excessive empty margins when more context is needed

lessonPractice.title: A blog article spans a 1600-pixel display, producing very long lines that make the next line hard to find. How should it change?

options.label: Constrain and center the article column, keep side whitespace, and retain left-aligned paragraphs
options.feedback: Stable line length reduces horizontal eye movement, and a centered narrow column keeps reading focused on wide screens.

options.label: Keep the article full-width and increase type size, line-height, and paragraph spacing
options.feedback: Type size does not stop line length growing with the viewport, so wide-screen return sweeps remain long.

options.label: Keep the full width but center-align every paragraph
options.feedback: Variable line starts make long-form reading harder and still do not constrain line length.

data.agentPrompt: Change the blog body to a centered narrow column with a readable maximum width tested for Chinese, English, type size, and devices. Keep paragraphs left-aligned, preserve mobile padding, and let code or images widen only when justified.
